---
title: "Fatigue"
---

[](`~slenderpy.fatigue.count_cycles`) counts the rainflow cycles (ASTM
E1049-85, without mean correction) of a position-dependent result at a
distance from a support:

```python
from slenderpy import fatigue

cycles = fatigue.count_cycles(res, "z", span, distance=0.089, support="right")
cycles.groupby("range")["count"].sum()
```

- The variable, for example `z`, `y`, `curvature` or `moment`, is read at the
  span fraction of the fatigue position by linear interpolation between the
  two stored positions around it: store the fatigue position itself in
  `Parameters.los` when possible.
- The result is a `pandas.DataFrame` with columns `range`, `mean` and `count`,
  one row per cycle (`count` 1) or half cycle (`count` 0.5), in extraction
  order.
- Both supports sit at a constant height, so counting `z` near a clamp gives
  the Poffenberger-Swart $Y_b$ ranges (89 mm from the clamp by convention);
  the means carry the static offset.
- Repeated equal samples are collapsed before counting, so a plateau, such
  as a run at rest, cannot hide cycles.

Stress models, S-N curves and damage are left to a dedicated package. See
the [wind fatigue example](examples/cable_wind_fatigue.qmd).
